gen-gf-funnel-display-gf-schibsted-grote: Expressive from the first letter, Funnel Display draws spaghetti-thin strokes of one width that look cut from strips. Schibsted Grotesk is the opposite in spirit, with big open e and a shapes and terminals that never close in.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-sintony: Wide, loud and well spaced, Goldman puts round forms on show like open parentheses. And Sintony follows with a chunky, tall midzone and curves that stay smooth instead of clogging up.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-sofia-sans: Sofia Sans reads modern and straight-lined, with no thick-and-thin shift and a clearly open side on its rounded letters. Grandstander keeps that same constant line width up top, but its tall x-height and held-open shapes give the pair a bolder, more expressive edge.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-osage: Noto Sans Osage reads approachable, its lowercase bowls puffed out to fill the line and its sweeping curves never closing up. Eater's dark spacing stays up top, so a long passage would feel friendly.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Futuristic and tile-like, Audiowide holds its line width through every turn. Noto Sans Armenian takes over below with tall, full c, s and z shapes and wide openings on its round letters, so a long passage would read warmly and without strain.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-ubuntu-sans: Round, loud and unshaded. Autour One has a clear channel into each curve, while Ubuntu Sans answers with tubular strokes like bent copper pipe, and washer-big lowercase eyes that make the pair feel solid.
gen-gf-funnel-display-gf-sofia-sans-semi: Sofia Sans Semi Condensed reads clean, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals in height and each curve entered through a big visible opening. And Funnel Display's spaghetti-like strokes sit beside it with a loose, expressive swagger the sans-serif never tries to copy.
gen-gf-gugi-fs-bespoke-sans: Distinctive is the word for Gugi, where stems and arches share one identical thickness and the lowercase climbs close to the capitals. Bespoke Sans is the sharper, more refined one, leaving generous space between its curve ends and the stem.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-abeezee: Gugi's lowercase climbs almost to the height of its capitals, and its terminals are cut open so the counters flow outward. ABeeZee sits lower and lighter, with a thickness like neon glass tubing.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-aldrich: Bold and distinctive, Gugi lets its tall lowercase nearly touch the capitals. Aldrich, a sans-serif with cupped round letters, makes a longer passage feel like tracing a single thick thread, modern and steady.
